newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-WEEKEND GAMES IN THE SPANISH LEAGUE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WEEKEND GAMES IN THE SPANISH LEAGUE.

text.p: Games scheduled for this weekend in the Spanish league championship (kick offs gmt, league standings in parentheses)

Atletico president Jesus Gil has hopes of seeing his side take Spain's second European Cup place and has warmed up for the game by exchanging insults with opposite number Eugenio Prieto. Carlos Aguilera and Delfi Geli are both doubtful for Gil's team.

Celta saw their season all but end on Wednesday with the semi-final Cup elimination by Betis, while injury-hit Tenerife are likely to be concentrating on impending UEFA Cup action which has meant the game has been brought forward.

Striker Ronaldo back from Brazil, and Vitor Baia is back in goal for a game in which Barcelona are clear favourites -- Sporting have lost 2-1 in each of their last three away games, and have lost on their last three visits to the Camp Nou.
Valencia welcome back midfielders Valery Karpin and Ariel Ortega and striker Goran Vlaovic from international duty, while Vicente Cantatore is expected to make changes in the Valladolid line-up.

Athletic have drawn 2-2 in their last three home games, while struggling Sevilla have brought back results from their last three away games with Bilbao. The game has been moved to San Sebastian because of the closure of the San Mames ground.
Logrones coach Carlos Aimar is expected to juggle his defence to cope with an attack that has turned around Extremadura's fortunes in fine style.

Racing, whose away form has fallen off recently, will be without injured striker Vladimir Bestchastnykh and face a Betis side still euphoric from reaching the Cup final. The game may be put back two hours because of Seville's high temperatures.
Espanyol Striker Florin Raduciou will miss the game because of injury, and could be replaced by teenager Raul Tamudo. Fellow strugglers Rayo will be without suspended midfielder Ezequiel Castillo.
Zaragoza have got a result from their last three games in the Riazor stadium, but will have to be at their best to cope with a Deportivo side that has taken 18 of their last 21 points.
Teenage star Raul Gonzalez is set make his 100th first division appearance in a game in which leaders Real will receive five foreign players back from international duty.
